title: Magnetic-field control of Fermi polaron fine structure and polarization in strained monolayer semiconductors
abstract: The theory of attractive Fermi polaron energy spectrum fine structure and polarization in doped two-dimensional semiconductors in external magnetic field is developed. Fermi polaron $g$ factor renormalization due to correlations with the valley-polarized Fermi sea of resident charge carriers is calculated. We study the competition between Zeeman and strain-induced splittings in monolayers under uniaxial strain. The control of strain, magnetic field and electron density allows continuous tuning of energy splitting and eigenstate polarization. Linearly polarized strain-induced split doublet exhibits quadratic Zeeman shift changing to linear Zeeman splitting with elliptical polarization with the increase of magnetic field. We identify a critical magnetic field above which resident charge carriers become fully valley polarized and only one circularly polarized Fermi polaron state remains. Within the Green's function approach we calculate energy levels and Stokes parameters of attractive Fermi polaron states and introduce a simplified effective two-level model allowing us to study analytically the interplay of Zeeman and pseudo-Zeeman splitting. We calculate absorption and reflection spectra, including circular and linear dichroism in the trion spectral range. These results show that real and strain-induced pseudomagnetic fields provide complementary tools for controlling the optical response of many-body excitonic quasiparticles in two-dimensional semiconductors.
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework to understand how the energy structure and polarization of Fermi polarons are controlled in 2D semiconductor monolayers using combined magnetic fields and mechanical strain. By calculating optical spectra via Green's functions, it demonstrates that these external parameters offer powerful, complementary tools for manipulating many-body excitonic quasiparticles.
main_problem: The theory develops the fine structure and polarization of Fermi polarons in doped two-dimensional semiconductors under the combined influence of external magnetic fields and uniaxial strain.
main_result: The study shows that controlling strain, magnetic field, and electron density allows continuous tuning of energy splitting and eigenstate polarization. Real and strain-induced pseudomagnetic fields provide complementary tools for controlling optical response.
method: The research employs the Green's function approach to calculate energy levels and Stokes parameters, supplemented by a simplified effective two-level model for analytical study.
model_or_system: The system involves excitons interacting with a Fermi sea of resident charge carriers in TMDC monolayers. The Hamiltonian incorporates terms for external magnetic fields (Zeeman shifts) and strain ($\hat{H}_s$).
key_observables: Energy levels, Stokes parameters, absorption/reflection spectra, circular and linear dichroism, and the polaron g factor renormalization.
important_parameters: External magnetic field ($B$), uniaxial strain, electron density, and critical magnetic fields leading to full valley polarization.
main_assumptions: Orbital effects of the magnetic field are neglected due to a small scattering time ($	au_e$). The analysis assumes $\mathbf{B}$ does not affect interaction parameters $V_1$ and $V_2$.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the intervalley Fermi polaron in W-based TMDC monolayers, showing Zeeman shifts both without and with an external magnetic field.
paper_structure: The theory builds from the non-interacting Hamiltonian ($\hat{H}_0$), incorporates magnetic field effects ($\hat{H}_B$) via the full Hamiltonian $\hat{H}$, and finally analyzes optical properties using Green's functions, culminating in spectral calculations for various regimes.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it treats open quantum systems dynamics (excitons coupled to a Fermi sea) under external fields, providing detailed predictions for magneto-optical responses that can be probed experimentally.
